A1_cube_vertices.png.caption: The unit cube generator: 24 vertices (4 per face, each with the face normal) and 36 indices (2 counter-clockwise triangles per face, diagonal 0-2). Indexed storage needs 720 B instead of 864 B.

A2_sphere_rings.png.caption: The sphere generator: 614 vertices on 9 rings x 36 slices per hemisphere, 1224 triangles; the normal of every vertex equals its normalised position, the southern half is the mirrored northern half.

A3_cylinder_cone.png.caption: Cylinder, cone and frustum come from one generator: two interleaved rings (bottom z = -0.5, top z = +0.5), side triangles, and a triangle fan per cap; a cone is simply top radius 0, the beam frustum has no caps.
A3_cylinder_cone.png.source: src/primitives/Cylinder.cpp: createCylinder(); Renderer.cpp lines 136-141 (which primitives exist)

A4_terrain_disc.png.caption: The terrain is a 36 m disc of 49921 vertices (130 rings x 384 slices) built like a cylinder cap and displaced by a height function; the left panel shows the ring structure on a coarse copy, the right panel the real triangles with the entrance-ramp hole.

A5_trs_worked_example.png.caption: Worked example for one real part, the tank's left turret cheek: the unit cube is scaled, rotated about Y and translated into its parent (the turret); the printed matrices are the scene's own, and T*R*S reproduces the node's local matrix.
A5_trs_worked_example.png.source: src/scene/Transform.h: Transform::matrix(); src/math/Math3D.cpp: rotateEulerYXZ(); Tank.cpp (node 'Turret cheek L')

A6_hierarchy_tank.png.caption: Scene-graph tree of the main battle tank (collapsed: identical siblings are merged): hull -> track groups / turret yaw -> gun pitch -> barrel recoil -> muzzle; each group multiplies its local matrix onto its children.
A6_hierarchy_tank.png.source: src/objects/Tank.cpp (rig), src/scene/SceneNode.h; counts from the live Scene

A6_hierarchy_uav.png.caption: Scene-graph trees of the UAV (gimbal yaw -> gimbal pitch carries lamp and thermal camera; rotors under their motor mounts; rounds on the launcher rails) and of the intruder rover.
A6_hierarchy_uav.png.source: src/objects/Uav.cpp, src/objects/Rover.cpp; counts from the live Scene

B1_barycentric.png.caption: Rasteriser interpolation: every pixel gets barycentric weights of its triangle; colours (Gouraud) or normals (Phong) are mixed with them, shown for a red / green / blue triangle. The right plot shows why the two differ: lighting is not linear in the normal.
B1_barycentric.png.source: OpenGL rasteriser; ShaderSources.cpp Gouraud / Phong varyings (TS_TERM_VARYINGS, line ~652)

B2_shading_models_coarse.png.caption: The same lit sphere mesh (sphere small) shaded three ways and compared with the exact analytic sphere; RMSE flat 0.143, Gouraud 0.118, Phong 0.112. Lighting uses the shader's own brdf() ported to Python.
B2_shading_models_coarse.png.source: ShaderSources.cpp: brdf() 113-139, computeLight() 143-196, compose() 561-566, kFlatGeom ~676; ShadersPostFx.cpp acesFitted() 387

B2_shading_models_real.png.caption: The same lit sphere mesh (sphere) shaded three ways and compared with the exact analytic sphere; RMSE flat 0.050, Gouraud 0.039, Phong 0.037. Lighting uses the shader's own brdf() ported to Python.
B2_shading_models_real.png.source: ShaderSources.cpp: brdf() 113-139, computeLight() 143-196, compose() 561-566, kFlatGeom ~676; ShadersPostFx.cpp acesFitted() 387

B3_lambert.png.caption: Lambert's cosine law as used for the diffuse term: intensity falls with cos of the angle between normal and light and is clamped at the terminator; the sphere at the right is lit by this term only.

C1_specular_lobes.png.caption: Surface shininess as a lobe: Blinn-Phong power n (v1) vs the GGX distribution (PBR); the right plot maps each v1 shininess to its derived roughness (roughness = 1 - log2(n)/8): GGX has a similar core width but a longer tail, which gives the soft halo around highlights.

C2_fresnel_geometry.png.caption: The G and F factors of the Cook-Torrance BRDF: Smith-Schlick shadowing, Schlick Fresnel for a dielectric (F0 = 0.04) and for the UAV's metal parts, and the resulting specular response when the view sweeps through the mirror direction for three roughness values.
C2_fresnel_geometry.png.source: ShaderSources.cpp brdf() lines 127-137, computeLight() line 148 (F0 = mix(0.04, albedo, metalness))

C3_specular_grid.png.caption: Roughness x metalness grid of lit spheres: low roughness gives a small bright highlight, high roughness a wide dim one; with metalness the diffuse term vanishes (1 - metalness) and F0 takes the albedo, so the highlight is tinted.

C4_practical_attenuation.png.caption: Practical lights fall off like an inverse square but are multiplied by a smooth window so they reach exactly zero at their range; spot lights add a smoothstep cone. The histogram lists the ranges of the lights actually built into the scene.
C4_practical_attenuation.png.source: ShaderSources.cpp practicalAttenuation() lines 90-100; ranges from Scene::practicalLights()

D1_ssr_raymarch.png.caption: How a puddle mirrors the scene: the reflected ray is stepped in world space, every sample is projected to the screen and its depth compared with the depth buffer; the first crossing (within a thickness) is refined by six bisections and the scene colour at that pixel is added, faded near the screen edge and for long marches.
D1_ssr_raymarch.png.source: ShadersPostFx.cpp kCombineFrag reflection() lines 44-81 (constants 0.04, 1.09, 0.03, thickness 0.15 + 0.04 t + 0.01 d, 6 bisections)

D2_fresnel_reflectivity.png.caption: Reflection strength: the Fresnel term makes grazing views mirror-like while the composite keeps at least 35 %; the lit pass decides per surface how much reflection it asks for (wet top faces, polished metal, puddles).

E1_planner_grids.png.caption: The four fields the infiltrating rover plans on: the free-cell occupancy grid, the exposure to the two UAVs, the per-rover noise field of two seeds and the resulting step cost (all dumped from the live HideController of the scene).

E2_flood_dijkstra.png.caption: Weighted MicroMouse flood field (Dijkstra from the objective) for two seeds with the same start and objective: the cost-to-go heat map, the steepest-descent cell route and the smoothed guide line; different noise fields make different routes.

E3_flood_bfs.png.caption: The v4 hiding behaviour: cells hidden from the UAV become goals, a breadth-first flood fill gives every free cell its step distance to cover, and the rover walks down the field (MicroMouse). Compared with the Dijkstra field, all steps cost the same.

E4_path_chaikin.png.caption: Chaikin corner cutting turns the staircase of grid cells into the smooth guide line the line follower tracks; three passes at 1/4 - 3/4 points, shown step by step on the real route.

E5_ir_sensors.png.caption: The line follower: five IR reflectance sensors on a bar 0.31 m ahead of the robot read whether they are over the 10 cm guide line; the weighted mean of the active offsets is the error that drives a PD controller and the differential-drive wheel speeds. Drawn from a real frame of a simulated drive.
E5_ir_sensors.png.source: src/ai/HideController.cpp: followLine() lines 308-366; constants kSensorForward, kSensorSpacing, kLineHalfWidth, kKp, kKd

E6_rover_trace.png.caption: A recorded drive of the intruder rover: its path over the occupancy grid and, for a 22 s window, the sensor bits, line error, PD steering command and left / right wheel speeds (error and PD command are reconstructed from the recorded sensor bits with the controller's formulas).
E6_rover_trace.png.source: src/ai/HideController.cpp followLine(); data from Scene::update() with figdata drive

F10_run_timeline.png.caption: Timeline of a simulated 90 s defence: the two UAVs' roles, the strike phase, the tracks' position uncertainty by life-cycle state, the game events (spotting, lock, launch, combined strike, explosion, kill) and the number of live rovers.
F10_run_timeline.png.source: src/scene/Scene.cpp update(); src/ai/Squad.cpp (data: figdata dumpSquad, 90 s, 30 Hz, vision from tests/test_squad.cpp syntheticBlobs)

F11_mission_waves.png.caption: Mission waves: wave n sends min(2 + n, 6) intruders (3, 4, 5, then 6), with the scoring and breach rules; the bars are produced by running the real Mission class.
F11_mission_waves.png.source: src/scene/Mission.cpp: startWave() lines 24-35, update() 37-75 (data: figdata dumpMission)

F1_threshold_histogram.png.caption: Adaptive threshold of the image stage: the histogram of a heat frame with the fixed floor 0.80, Otsu's threshold (maximum of the between-class variance) and the threshold actually used, their maximum. A hot frame raises Otsu above the floor; a cold one leaves the floor in charge.
F1_threshold_histogram.png.source: src/vision/CvPipeline.cpp: otsuThreshold() lines 9-32, detectTargets() lines 114-122 (synthetic 320x240 frame through the real functions)

F2_cv_stages.png.caption: The image stage on a synthetic 320x240 heat frame, run through the real functions: threshold, despeckle, labelling, features and the target filter; the table lists why each component is accepted or rejected.

F3_union_find.png.caption: Two-pass connected-component labelling with union-find on a small 12 x 7 mask: pass 1 gives provisional labels and records that two of them touch (red pixels); pass 2 resolves every label to its root. The picture is checked against the real labelComponents() output.

F4_blob_moments.png.caption: Blob features from image moments: centroid, bounding box and the principal axes of the pixel distribution (eigenvectors of the second central moments) give the orientation and the elongation used to reject thin streaks; values were recomputed and checked against the real detectTargets().

F5_kalman_filter.png.caption: The track filter on a rover driving straight, turning and driving straight: noisy ground measurements, the Kalman estimate with 2-sigma ellipses, the position error against the filter's own uncertainty, and the velocity estimate converging from the unknown initial value. Run through the real MultiTracker.
F5_kalman_filter.png.source: src/vision/MultiTracker.cpp: predict() lines 21-46, kalmanUpdate() 60-82 (data: figdata dumpKalman)

F6_gating_hungarian.png.caption: Data association for one UAV frame: each track predicts where it should be, the chi-square gate (d^2 < 9.21) removes impossible pairs, and the Hungarian algorithm picks the pairing with the smallest total Mahalanobis cost (note m0 and m1 both fit track 3 but only the globally cheaper pairing wins).
F6_gating_hungarian.png.source: src/vision/MultiTracker.cpp: mahalanobis2() 48-56, hungarian() 84-137, update() 175-190 (data: figdata dumpAssociation)

F7_triangulation.png.caption: Two-view triangulation: each UAV's pixel becomes a ray, the fused fix is the midpoint of the shortest segment between the rays (residual = segment length); Monte Carlo over pointing noise shows it beats a single ground-plane ray and that a wing UAV at about 90 degrees gives the best geometry.
F7_triangulation.png.source: src/vision/MultiTracker.cpp: triangulate() lines 139-153; Squad.cpp measurement sigma 0.12 + 0.015 r (data: figdata dumpTriangulation)

F8_squad_state_machine.png.caption: The squad's state machines: the UAV roles (patrol, track, lead / wing, search and back) and the strike phases (tracking, planned, inbound, reacquire), with the lock times and distances that trigger the transitions.
F8_squad_state_machine.png.source: src/ai/Squad.cpp: update() 220-327, planStrike() 176-218; Squad.h constants kSquadLeadLock etc.

F9_time_on_target.png.caption: Time-on-target: the squad predicts each round's flight time from the distance with a two-phase model (accelerating launch, then 60 m/s, detonating 0.5 m short), launches the farther UAV first and the nearer one later so the blasts coincide; the right plot shows the model against the simulated missile and the distances of this strike.
F9_time_on_target.png.source: src/ai/Squad.cpp: roundFlightTime() lines 43-50, planStrike() 193-212; src/scene/Combat.h kMissile* (data: figdata dumpSquad / dumpFlight)

G1_render_pipeline.png.caption: Overview of one rendered frame: scene graph to world matrices, shadow maps and pre-pass, ambient occlusion and fog, the HDR object pass with Flat / Gouraud / Phong lighting, then SSR, temporal anti-aliasing, exposure, bloom / depth of field and the final filmic composite (or the thermal sensor model).
G1_render_pipeline.png.source: src/rendering/RendererFrame.cpp (frame order), ShadersPostFx.cpp header comment lines 1-4

G2_cv_pipeline.png.caption: From heat pixels to a shared track picture and a coordinated strike: image stage (threshold, despeckle, labelling, features, target filter), ground ray, gating and assignment, Kalman update with optional two-view triangulation, track life cycle, and the squad logic.
G2_cv_pipeline.png.source: src/vision/CvPipeline.h header comment, MultiTracker.h header comment, Squad.h header comment

G3_game_loop.png.caption: One simulation step: input, vision blobs, squad decisions, controllable objects, mission waves, intruder planning and driving, combat and effects, then world matrices and rendering; the rendered thermal images become the next frame's vision input.
G3_game_loop.png.source: src/scene/Scene.cpp: Scene::update() lines 353-445; src/app/App.cpp update() lines 262-285

H1_daycycle_curves.png.caption: Day cycle from the exported 24 h grid (97 rows): sun elevation with the phase thresholds and the four phase events, and the lighting quantities that follow it (key intensity, daylight weight, practical lamps, exposure key, mean cloud shadow); bottom: the key-light hue (sun reddening by air mass, moon blue at night).

H2_kasten_young.png.caption: Left: the Kasten--Young air mass against the plane-parallel 1/sin(e), which diverges at the horizon. Right: the per-channel sun transmittance relative to the zenith path and the normalised disc colour (strip): white at noon, orange-red near the horizon.
H2_kasten_young.png.source: src/scene/DayCycle.cpp airMass / sunTransmittance (ported), kSunOpticalDepth from DayCycle.h

H3_catmull_rom.png.caption: Left: Catmull--Rom curves through the same unevenly spaced control points; the uniform parameterisation overshoots next to the short edges, the centripetal one stays tight without cusps. Right: curvature along the centripetal curve and the walking speed it allows (soldier walk speed 1.3 m/s).
H3_catmull_rom.png.source: src/math/Spline.cpp evalSegment / curvatureAtDistance and src/scene/Garrison.cpp stepRoute (ported); control points illustrative

H4_gait_cycle.png.caption: The walk cycle as the program computes it: joint angles over one cycle (left stance shaded), the ankle path relative to the hip (flat world-locked stance, cycloid swing with lift) and stick figures rebuilt by forward kinematics from the same angles.
H4_gait_cycle.png.source: build/scene_export.json v6.garrison.gait (gaitPose, footInPelvis, legIK in src/scene/Gait.cpp)

H5_two_link_ik.png.caption: Two-link IK by the law of cosines: the knee angle from the triangle (hip, knee, ankle), the hip angle from the direction to the target plus the triangle's angle at the hip. The same solver (with a pole vector instead of the planar knee rule) poses the arms on the rifle.
H5_two_link_ik.png.source: src/scene/Gait.cpp legIK / legFK (ported); thigh and shin lengths from v6.garrison.gait.walk

H6_spawn_ring.png.caption: Random intruder routes: a spawn bearing drawn uniformly on the ring outside the gate-road gap, up to three via points in a sector around the spawn bearing (driven outermost first, so the chain closes in on the camp), then the objective. Right: the rejection sampler gives a flat bearing histogram with an empty gap at north.
H6_spawn_ring.png.source: src/scene/Mission.cpp randomRoute (ported, Python RNG); constants from v6.random_routes and BaseLayout.h

H7_pd_netd.png.caption: Real-CV statistics against the temporal noise level (NETD), full sensor model (PSF, fixed pattern after NUC, stuck pixels): detection probability of a rover (full size and half size), person recognition, false targets and persons misread as targets per frame; crosses: the same at the default NETD without NUC. Bottom: the synthetic test crop at each NETD with the classified blobs (target = cyan, person = green).
